chapter: Learning drums and recording on the Coast
title: Learning drums from his brother Bud on a lard bucket
summary: Smith recaps Lovett's life since 1894 and asks how he began; he copied his brother James 'Bud' Lovett on a lard bucket and cans.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: Right. I'm just -- I think that's a fairly good chronological sequence of events, Babe. Let's see. Born in Pineville, Louisiana in 1894 and sitting in here in the After Hours 81 years later with many, many rooms inbetween and lots of music.

I know. Speaking of music maybe we ought to get on some of the questions relative to music, before we get on personalities. Over the years with your own bands probably more than with other bands. Oh, prior to getting onto some of the questions relative to music and society as you knew it over the years, tell us how you started on drums, how did you start to play drums, Baby?
Well, I -- my brother started me.
James Lovett. We called him Bud for you know --

That's right. He taught me how to play. Well, I -- he didn't teach me but I could hear him practicing at home there, you know, and he has fine drums, had his fine drums set up. Man, I'd get me a lard bucket and go out and --
Yeah, lard bucket. And some chair around and -- any kind of stick I could find, see, and I'd hear
him make something on his and I'd try to make it on my cans.
He used to tell me to stop, I'd say okay. When I was thinking about it he told me to stop, so that's the way I learned.
